passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.
passages.sermon: This psalm is for the choirmaster.\r\nThe sons of Korah wrote this psalm.\r\nThis psalm is a Maskil, which means it is a song of instruction.

passages.text: As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this song.
They gave it to the choirmaster.
A deer needs water.
A deer pants for streams of water.
My soul is like that deer.
My soul longs for you, God.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לִבְנֵי־ קֹֽרַח׃ כְּאַיָּ֗ל תַּעֲרֹ֥ג עַל־ אֲפִֽיקֵי־ מָ֑יִם כֵּ֤ן נַפְשִׁ֨י תַעֲרֹ֖ג אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When shall I come and appear in God’s presence?
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this song.
They sing to God.
My soul thirsts for God.
God is the living God.
I ask, “When will I come before God?”
I want to see God’s face.
passages.original: צָמְאָ֬ה נַפְשִׁ֨י׀ לֵאלֹהִים֮ לְאֵ֪ל חָ֥י מָתַ֥י אָב֑וֹא וְ֝אֵרָאֶ֗ה פְּנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: My tears have been my food both day and night, while men ask me all day long, “Where is your God?”
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
They sing to God.
I cry often.
My tears do not stop.
I weep in the day.
I weep in the night.
I have no other food but my tears.
People speak to me all day.
They ask me, “Where is your God?”
passages.original: הָֽיְתָה־ לִּ֬י דִמְעָתִ֣י לֶ֭חֶם יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה בֶּאֱמֹ֥ר אֵלַ֥י כָּל־ הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: These things come to mind as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the multitude, leading the procession to the house of God with shouts of joy and praise.
passages.sermon:
The writer is a person who longs deeply for God.
This person remembers important things.
These memories come when the person pours out his soul.
He remembers walking with a large crowd.
He led the people in a procession.
They went to the house of God together.
They shouted with joy.
They gave praise and thanks to God.
The crowd celebrated as they went.
passages.original: אֵ֤לֶּה אֶזְכְּרָ֨ה׀ וְאֶשְׁפְּכָ֬ה עָלַ֨י׀ נַפְשִׁ֗י כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר׀ בַּסָּךְ֮ אֶדַּדֵּ֗ם עַד־ בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים בְּקוֹל־ רִנָּ֥ה וְתוֹדָ֗ה הָמ֥וֹן חוֹגֵֽג׃

passages.text: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to his own soul.
He feels sadness and trouble inside himself.
He asks, “Why are you downcast, my soul?”
He asks, “Why is there unease within me?”
He tells his soul to hope in God.
He says he will praise God again.
He trusts God will save him with His presence.
passages.original: מַה־ תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ וַתֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ ע֥וֹד אוֹדֶ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: O my God, my soul despairs within me. Therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon— even from Mount Mizar.
passages.sermon:
My God, my soul feels despair within me.
I feel deep sadness inside.
Because of this, I remember You.
I remember You while I am in the land of Jordan.
I remember You from the peaks of Hermon.
I remember You even from Mount Mizar.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י עָלַי֮ נַפְשִׁ֪י תִשְׁתּ֫וֹחָ֥ח עַל־ כֵּ֗ן אֶ֭זְכָּרְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יַרְדֵּ֑ן וְ֝חֶרְמוֹנִ֗ים מֵהַ֥ר מִצְעָֽר׃

passages.text: Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.
passages.sermon:
God is present and powerful.
I feel overwhelmed.
One deep place calls to another deep place.
The sound of Your waterfalls is loud.
Your breakers have crashed over me.
Your waves have swept over me.
passages.original: תְּהֽוֹם־ אֶל־ תְּה֣וֹם ק֭וֹרֵא לְק֣וֹל צִנּוֹרֶ֑יךָ כָּֽל־ מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְ֝גַלֶּ֗יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is my God.
The LORD commands His loving devotion during the day.
At night, His song stays with me.
This song is a prayer.
I pray to the God who gives me life.
passages.original: יוֹמָ֤ם׀ יְצַוֶּ֬ה יְהוָ֨ה׀ חַסְדּ֗וֹ וּ֭בַלַּיְלָה שִׁירָהּ עִמִּ֑י תְּ֝פִלָּ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל חַיָּֽי׃

passages.text: I say to God my Rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?”
passages.sermon:
God is my Rock.
I speak to Him.
I ask God, "Why have You forgotten me?"
I ask God, "Why must I walk in sorrow?"
The enemy oppresses me.
Because of this, I am sad.
passages.original: אוֹמְרָ֤ה׀ לְאֵ֥ל סַלְעִי֮ לָמָ֪ה שְׁכַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה־ קֹדֵ֥ר אֵלֵ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: Like the crushing of my bones, my enemies taunt me, while they say to me all day long, “Where is your God?”
passages.sermon:
My enemies attack me.
Their words hurt me deeply.
Their insults feel like my bones are breaking.
All day long, they speak against me.
They say to me, "Where is your God?"
passages.original: בְּרֶ֤צַח׀ בְּֽעַצְמוֹתַ֗י חֵרְפ֥וּנִי צוֹרְרָ֑י בְּאָמְרָ֥ם אֵלַ֥י כָּל־ הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks to his own soul.
He asks his soul a question.
He says, "Why are you downcast, my soul?"
He asks, "Why is there unease within me?"
He tells his soul to hope in God.
He says he will praise God again.
He calls God his Savior.
He calls God his God.
passages.original: מַה־ תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה־ תֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי׃
